summary: In March 2026, 'North' Electronics has only 140 units sold across 35 rows, far below every other region/category combination shown, and it is split from a lowercase 'north' Electronics group with 5 rows and 26 units. The missing rows and very low sales are consistent with sustained out-of-stock conditions.
observations: North Electronics reports only 140 units sold, versus 1,528 in South, 1,598 in East, 1,717 in West, 1,976 in Northeast, and 2,058 in Central Electronics.
North Electronics appears in 35 rows, while the fully stocked region/category groups appear in 40 rows.

A separate lowercase "north" Electronics group appears with 5 rows and 26 units; combined with "North" Electronics this gives 40 rows and 166 units, matching the 40-row pattern but still far below other Electronics regions.
By contrast, North Grocery, Apparel, and Home sell 1,568, 1,909, and 1,389 units respectively, indicating the weakness is specific to Electronics rather than all North categories.
The largest North Electronics sales gap is against Central Electronics, which sold 2,058 units, approximately 14 times the North Electronics total.
caveats: The result only shows sales and row counts; it does not directly prove stockout causes because no inventory or stockout fields are queried.
Region names appear inconsistently as "North" and "north", so reported North totals may be understated unless the labels are normalized.
The query filters March using week_start LIKE '2026-03%', so any rows outside that week_start string format would be excluded.
Results are truncated to 25 rows, so the displayed category totals may not represent the complete data.
The relationship between row count and weeks cannot be confirmed from the result alone because the week_start values are not shown.
